explanation: `Real.cosh` and `Real.sinh` are by definition the real parts of `Complex.cosh` and `Complex.sinh` applied to the coerced real (`Real.cosh x = (Complex.cosh ↑x).re`, `Real.sinh x = (Complex.sinh ↑x).re`, see Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Trigonometric.lean), and the generic transfer lemma `HasDerivAt.real_of_complex` (Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/RealDeriv.lean:47) turns complex differentiability of `e` at `↑x` with derivative `e'` into real differentiability of `fun t => (e t).re` with derivative `e'.re`. Instantiating `Complex.hasDerivAt_cosh` at `↑x` and applying `real_of_complex` gives exactly `HasDerivAt Real.cosh (Real.sinh x) x`, in one line — which is precisely how the library proves it. No other Mathlib declaration states the real statement directly (grep for `hasDerivAt_cosh`/`deriv_cosh` yields only the complex version, the targets, and circular wrappers such as `Real.HasDerivAt.cosh`/`Real.deriv_cosh`, which are proved from this theorem).
